unit.can_do_en: talk about the seasons and the weather over a year.

brief.situation_en: Maria and Leena look out of the window.

judge.reason: kato/katso is only a register difference; the content is the same.

lines.speaker: Leena
lines.text_puhe: Joo, eka lumi! Onks tää sun eka kerta?
lines.text_kirja: Kyllä, ensimmäinen lumi! Onko tämä sinun ensimmäinen kertasi?
lines.gloss_en: Yes, the first snow! Is this your first time?

judge.reason: Joo/kyllä, eka/ensimmäinen, tää/tämä and sun/sinun are all register variants; the meaning is identical.

lines.speaker: Leena
lines.text_puhe: Odota vaan, talvel on vielä enemmän lunta.
lines.text_kirja: Odota vain, talvella on vielä enemmän lunta.
lines.gloss_en: Just wait, in winter there's even more snow.

judge.reason: talvel is spoken for talvella (in winter); vaan/vain is the same word in a different register.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Is it colder here than in Lapland?

judge.reason: Lapis is colloquial for Lapissa (in Lapland); ku/kuin is a register difference. The question is the same.
Both say no, Lapland is much colder; Lapis/Lapissa is a register difference.
mä/minä and tarviin/tarvitsen are register differences; the warmer coat is the same.
hanskat and käsineet both mean gloves or hand coverings; this is a register or vocabulary difference, and the pipon (hat) is the same.

forms.why_en: This is how you tell someone to look: katso. Speech drops the s: kato.
sataa, to rain or fall. Finnish needs no 'it' here: Sataa lunta, it is snowing.
Lumi becomes lunta for some snow: m changes to n and -ta is added.
Yes. In everyday speech people often say joo instead.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Means 'is...?'. The question ending -ko turns 'on' (is) into a question.
Speech shortens tämä to tää. Books write tämä.
Sinä with -n for 'your': sinun. Speech shortens it to sun.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for your
forms.why_en: Books add -si for 'your': kertasi. Speech drops it and says sun kerta.
